newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to propose $3.9 billion plan for D.C..
newsitem.headline: Clinton to propose $3.9 billion plan for D.C..

text.p: President Clinton will propose a $3.9 billion, five-year plan to help rescue the financially distressed Washington D.C. government, the White House said Tuesday.

The package of initiatives calls for the federal government to help the District of Columbia pay medical bills for its poorest citizens, assume responsibility for the city's prisons and courts as well as a $4.4 billion pension fund liability.

Senior U.S. officials were to unveil details of the plan later on Tuesday. It is to be included in Clinton's budget proposal for the 1998 fiscal year starting next Oct. 1. He is to submit his budget blueprint to Congress Feb. 6.
"This nation's capital city is in distress, and it's important that the American people understand that, and understand what we are going to do about it," said White House spokesman Mike McCurry.
He said the $3.9 billion, five-year plan would replace the federal government's annual $660 million payment to the District, representing a net gain of $339 million over the period.

It will go toward prison renovation and construction, operation of prison facilities and the courts, as well as start rebuilding the city's transportation infrastructure, and improve the city's ability to collect taxes, McCurry said.
